mainTopic: Is טומאת משקין דאורייתא? רבי יהודה's retraction and רבי יוסי's source in the word 'יטמא'
overview: The גמרא first asks whether רבי יהודה fully gave up his view that liquids make things impure on a Torah level, or only gave it up for vessels (כלים) but not for foods (אוכלין). It tests this with a משנה about a cow that drank מי חטאת, where רבי יהודה says the water is 'nullified in its innards' (בטלו במעיה). The proof is pushed off: 'nullified' may mean only from the severe impurity, and the whole משנה is read as רבי יהודה's view with words missing (חסורי מיחסרא). רב אשי gives another answer: the water is fully nullified because it becomes a foul liquid (משקה סרוח), so the case proves nothing either way. The גמרא then turns to רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, who say a doubtful impure liquid makes foods impure but not vessels. ריש לקיש explains that רבי יוסי follows רבי עקיבא, who reads 'יִטְמָא' (will be impure) as 'יְטַמֵּא' (will make impure). Using the two יטמא's in the פסוק, the גמרא shows that the second one teaches that liquids make foods impure. It is not about other liquids, as רב פפא and רבינא prove. It is not about vessels either, because of a קל וחומר and because the פסוק speaks only of liquids made impure through a vessel.

steps.title: Attempted proof that רבי יהודה retracted completely
steps.stepSummary: The cited source ends with רבי יהודה's words 'בטלו במעיה.' The גמרא argues: if רבי יהודה still held that liquids make foods impure מדאורייתא, why would the water be nullified entirely?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They are nullified in its innards.' Now, if you think רבי יהודה changed his mind only about vessels, but about foods he still agrees with רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, why does he say the water is nullified in its innards completely?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יהודה's words in the משנה about the cow. Then it uses those words to try to prove that רבי יהודה gave up his whole view about liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose רבי יהודה still held that liquids make foods impure on a Torah level. Then the swallowed water should still count as an impure liquid in some way. Saying it is 'completely nullified' sounds like he no longer holds any Torah-level impurity of liquids at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the waters) are nullified in its (the cow's) innards
It enters your mind / you might think

steps.confusionAlert: The first two words, 'בטלו במעיה,' are not a new statement. They are the end of רבי יהודה's words in the משנה about the פרה that drank מי חטאת, which was quoted on the previous amud.

phrases.english: They are nullified in its innards.
phrases.notes: End of רבי יהודה's quote in the משנה about the cow that drank מי חטאת.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that it was from vessels that he retracted,
phrases.notes: He backed off his view that liquids make vessels impure on a Torah level.

phrases.english: but regarding foods

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: he holds like Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: They hold that liquids make food impure on a Torah level.

phrases.english: why are they nullified in its innards entirely?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מִכֵּלִים הוּא דַּהֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the end of the quoted משנה (on the previous amud) as evidence about how far רבי יהודה retracted.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה retracted completely and holds that טומאת משקין is entirely דרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה of פרה: בטלו במעיה.

steps.title: Spelling out the proof: at least the lighter impurity should remain
steps.stepSummary: Even if the water loses its severe impurity, it should still give the lighter impurity of an ordinary liquid. Since it does not, רבי יהודה must hold that the impurity of liquids is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that the waters do not give the severe impurity, at least let them give the light impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the proof from step 1 more sharply. It separates the severe impurity of מי חטאת from the regular light impurity that any liquid has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה חמורה is the special status of מי חטאת as an אב הטומאה, which makes even a person or vessel impure. טומאה קלה is the regular impurity of a liquid, which makes food impure. If רבי יהודה held the light impurity was דאורייתא, it should survive. Since 'completely nullified' wipes out even that, it suggests he holds it is only דרבנן, and the חכמים did not decree in this unusual case.

keyTerms.meaning: Severe impurity (of מי חטאת as an אב הטומאה, affecting people and vessels)
Light impurity (like a regular liquid, affecting food)

phrases.english: Granted that they do not transmit severe impurity,
let them at least transmit light impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the word 'לגמרי' (completely) in step 1 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה denies any Torah-level impurity of liquids.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The waters lose even their light impurity according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Rejection: 'nullified' means only from the severe impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. Maybe 'בטלו במעיה' means the water loses only its severe impurity, but it still gives light impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they are nullified in its innards' mean? They are nullified from severe impurity, but they still transmit light impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading רבי יהודה's words more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on 'nullified' meaning nullified from everything. If it means only the severe impurity, then the light impurity stays. So רבי יהודה could still hold that liquids make food impure מדאורייתא, and nothing has been proven.

keyTerms.meaning: What, too, is the meaning of...? (reinterpreting a phrase)

phrases.english: What, too, is 'they are nullified in its innards'?
They are nullified from severe impurity,
but they do transmit light impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 1-2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that רבי יהודה denies all Torah-level impurity of liquids.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'בטלו' means nullified completely. It may mean nullified only from the severe impurity.

steps.title: Problem with the rejection: what would the תנא קמא hold?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה means the water loses only its severe impurity, then the תנא קמא must hold that it keeps even the severe impurity. But the תנא קמא only says 'its meat is impure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that the תנא קמא holds the waters transmit severe impurity too. But he teaches only 'its meat is impure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the narrow reading from step 3. That reading creates a problem with the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument needs two sides. If רבי יהודה says 'only light impurity,' the תנא קמא must be saying 'severe impurity too.' But 'its meat is impure' describes only the ordinary, light impurity of the meat. It does not describe the severe impurity of מי חטאת. So the two opinions would end up saying the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) תנא in the משנה

phrases.english: This implies that the first Tanna holds:
they transmit severe impurity too,
but he teaches 'its flesh is impure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reinterpretation given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'בטלו במעיה' refers only to טומאה חמורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the תנא קמא would have to hold that the waters keep severe impurity. But his wording, 'its meat is impure,' points only to light impurity, so no real disagreement is left.

steps.title: Answer: the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, with words missing
steps.stepSummary: The whole משנה follows רבי יהודה, and words are missing from it. Read correctly, it says: the meat is impure with light impurity but not with severe impurity, because רבי יהודה says the waters are nullified in its innards.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and it has words missing. This is what it teaches: A cow that drank מי חטאת, its meat is impure. When was this said? About light impurity. But about severe impurity, no, because רבי יהודה says: they are nullified in its innards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem from step 4. There are not two opinions here at all. The whole משנה is one view, רבי יהודה's, and the גמרא rebuilds its missing words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה is not a disagreement, the תנא קמא does not need to hold that the severe impurity stays. 'Its meat is impure' means light impurity. 'בטלו במעיה' explains why there is no severe impurity. So the narrow reading from step 3 stands, and the attempted proof that רבי יהודה fully retracted is defeated.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing words (the text is incomplete)
And this is what it teaches
Purification waters (with ashes of the פרה אדומה)
In what case is this said?

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי יהודה holds that swallowed מי חטאת lose only their severe impurity and still make the meat impure with light impurity. So this source does not prove he fully retracted his view on טומאת משקין.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'חסורי מיחסרא' is a common tool in the גמרא. When it is used, a משנה that looks like a disagreement can turn out to be one opinion with an explanation attached.

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and it is incomplete, and this is what it teaches:
a cow that drank purification waters —
its flesh is impure.
In what case is this said? Regarding light impurity,
but regarding severe impurity — no,
as Rabbi Yehuda says: they are nullified in its innards.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4, which keeps the rejection of step 3 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reconstruction (חסורי מיחסרא): the משנה is reread as one opinion, not a disagreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is a disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה, so the תנא קמא must hold that the severe impurity remains.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה: the meat has light impurity only, and the severe impurity is nullified in the innards.

steps.title: רב אשי: The water is fully nullified because it becomes foul
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the water really does lose all impurity inside the cow. The reason is that it becomes a foul liquid, not that liquid impurity is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, the water is nullified in the cow's innards completely. This is because it has become a spoiled, foul liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different way to explain רבי יהודה's words 'בטלו במעיה.' He agrees the water loses all impurity, but he gives a new reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 had said the water loses only its severe impurity, and that forced us to rewrite the משנה. רב אשי avoids that. He says the water loses everything because swallowed water becomes a foul liquid, and a foul liquid cannot carry impurity at all. So the case proves nothing about whether liquid impurity is דאורייתא or דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (I keep the original reading)
A foul, spoiled liquid, which cannot become impure or make other things impure
In its innards (inside the cow's body)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, the water in the cow is pure because it became a foul liquid. The case gives no proof about whether liquid impurity is דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying that liquid impurity is only דרבנן. He gives a completely different reason, so the original proof from Steps 1–2 falls away.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, they are nullified in its innards completely,
phrases.notes: He takes 'בטלו' at face value: all impurity is gone.

phrases.english: because it has become a foul liquid.
phrases.notes: A foul liquid is no longer a 'liquid' for purity laws.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to Steps 3–5. Instead of rewriting the משנה, it explains the full nullification with a new reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from Steps 1–2 that רבי יהודה holds liquid impurity is only דרבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The full nullification comes from the water becoming foul, not from the status of liquid impurity.

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: Impure for foods, pure for vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the view of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון in the ברייתא about doubtful liquids. Such a liquid makes foods impure, but vessels stay pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: With regard to foods, they are impure. With regard to vessels, they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion from the ברייתא about a case of doubt involving impure liquids. This sets up the explanation that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we are unsure whether a liquid made something impure, these תנאים split the ruling. Foods that touched it are impure, but vessels that touched it are pure. The split hints that liquids making foods impure is a Torah law, while liquids making vessels impure is only rabbinic, so we can be lenient in a doubt about vessels.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
With regard to foods, they are impure,
with regard to vessels, they are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another opinion in the ברייתא about liquid impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful impure liquid makes foods impure but does not make vessels impure.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי יוסי follows רבי עקיבא's reading of 'יטמא'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that רבי יוסי follows his teacher רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא reads 'יִטְמָא' (will be impure) as 'יְטַמֵּא' (will make impure).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of ריש לקיש: רבי יוסי said this following the approach of רבי עקיבא, his teacher, who reads 'יִטְמָא' (it will be impure) as 'יְטַמֵּא' (it will make others impure).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי יוסי's ruling comes from. He follows רבי עקיבא's way of reading a key word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same Hebrew letters can be read 'יִטְמָא' (it becomes impure) or 'יְטַמֵּא' (it makes others impure). רבי עקיבא reads it the second way. So a liquid making foods impure comes straight from the Torah, and that is why רבי יוסי is strict about foods even in a case of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: It will be impure (it receives impurity)
It will make impure (it gives impurity)

steps.confusionAlert: 'יִטְמָא' and 'יְטַמֵּא' use the same letters. The only difference is the vowels, and that changes the meaning from 'becomes impure' to 'makes impure.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said it following the approach of Rabbi Akiva, his teacher,
who interprets 'it will be impure' as 'it will make impure.'
phrases.notes: It's the same Hebrew letters, just read with different vowels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source behind רבי יוסי's ruling in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי follows רבי עקיבא, who reads 'יטמא' as 'it will make impure.'

steps.title: Proof that רבי עקיבא reads 'יטמא' as 'it makes impure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי עקיבא taught this reading. From it he learned that a second-level loaf makes ordinary food third-level impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: On that day, רבי עקיבא taught: 'And every earthenware vessel into which any of them falls…' The verse does not say 'it is impure' but 'it will be impure,' meaning it will make others impure. This teaches that a second-level loaf makes a third-level impurity, even in ordinary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where we know that רבי עקיבא reads 'יטמא' as 'it will make impure.' It brings a משנה that records his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'טָמֵא' (it is impure). Instead it says 'יִטְמָא,' and רבי עקיבא reads it as 'יְטַמֵּא,' meaning the item makes others impure. From this he learns that a loaf with second-level impurity (שני) passes on third-level impurity (שלישי), even to ordinary food (חולין).

keyTerms.meaning: On that day (the day רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was appointed נשיא)
Third-level impurity in ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: As we learned: On that day Rabbi Akiva taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכׇל כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ אֲשֶׁר יִפֹּל מֵהֶם וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: 'And every earthenware vessel into which any of them falls, etc.'
It does not say 'it is impure' but 'it will be impure':
it will make others impure.
It teaches about a second-level loaf
that it makes a third-level impurity in ordinary food.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 8 by showing where רבי עקיבא's reading is recorded.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא reads 'יטמא' as 'it will make impure'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of 'בו ביום' about ויקרא יא:לג

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי read the verse about liquids?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this reading applies here, to liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, how does he interpret it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where in the פסוק about liquids רבי יוסי finds this reading. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's teaching was about an earthenware vessel. Our case is about liquids, so the גמרא needs to find the 'יטמא' in the פסוק that speaks about liquids.

phrases.english: And here, how does he interpret it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how Step 9's reading applies to liquids.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches, by this reading, that liquids make foods impure

steps.title: The liquids verse: 'יטמא' teaches liquids make foods impure
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the פסוק 'And every drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall be impure.' Read as 'יְטַמֵּא,' it teaches that liquids make foods impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And every drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall be impure.' Read it as 'shall make impure,' meaning it makes foods impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting the פסוק about liquids and applying רבי עקיבא's reading to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יטמא' appears in the liquids פסוק (ויקרא יא:לד). Read as 'יְטַמֵּא,' it means the liquid gives impurity, specifically to foods. That makes it a Torah law that liquids make foods impure, which explains why רבי יוסי is strict about foods even in a doubt.

phrases.english: 'And every drink that may be drunk'
'in any vessel shall be impure':
read it as 'shall make impure,' to make foods impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מַשְׁקֶה אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁתֶה בְּכׇל כְּלִי יִטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The liquids פסוק, read as 'יְטַמֵּא,' teaches that liquids make foods impure by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah source for רבי יוסי's view that liquids make foods impure. It explains why he is strict about foods but lenient about vessels in Step 7.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means liquids make only other liquids impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading. Perhaps 'יְטַמֵּא' means the liquid makes other liquids impure, not foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means to make foods impure, or perhaps it only means to make liquids impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the reading from Step 11. It asks whether 'makes impure' might refer to other liquids instead of foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יְטַמֵּא' tells us the liquid gives impurity, but it does not say to what. Since the פסוק is talking about liquids, maybe it means other liquids. If so, the source for liquids making foods impure would be lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say (introduces a possible alternative reading)

phrases.english: Do you say it means to make foods impure,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין?
phrases.english: or perhaps it only means to make liquids impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אוֹכָלִין, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'יְטַמֵּא' in the liquids פסוק means making foods impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'makes impure' does not say what it makes impure. It could just as well mean other liquids.

steps.title: The reply begins: 'That is not how it was'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the alternative reading by saying 'לא כך היה.' The full explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said in reply: That is not how it was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge from Step 12 by saying that the 'other liquids' reading is wrong. This line opens the answer, and the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא כך היה' rejects the idea that the פסוק means liquids make only other liquids impure. That keeps the reading that liquids make foods impure. The reasons are given in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not how it was (the suggested reading is rejected)

phrases.english: You said in reply: That is not how it was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'liquids only' reading is rejected. The explanation continues next.

steps.title: What does 'That was not so' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the short phrase 'לא כך היה' that was used to reject the alternative reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'That was not so' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the short rejection 'לא כך היה' actually means. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13 the alternative reading (liquids make liquids impure) was brushed aside with just three words and no reason. The גמרא now wants the logic behind that rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean
That was not so (a short rejection)

phrases.english: What does 'That was not so' mean?
phrases.notes: The גמרא wants to know why the idea was rejected back in Step 13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the rejection given in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind 'לא כך היה'. Why can't 'יִטְמָא' mean liquids make other liquids impure?

steps.title: רב פפא: impurity never makes the same kind of thing impure
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that we never find an impurity that makes an item of its own kind impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We have never found an impurity that makes something like itself impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the rejection. In the laws of טומאה, an impure item never passes impurity to the same kind of item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'יִטְמָא' meant that liquid makes other liquid impure, liquid would be passing impurity to its own kind. That pattern does not exist anywhere in the laws of טומאה, so the reading is rejected. That leaves the reading that liquids make foods impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Something like itself, of the same kind

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We have not found any impurity
that makes something like itself impure.
phrases.notes: Liquid making liquid impure would be 'like itself'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא מָצִינוּ טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No impurity ever makes the same kind of item impure. So liquid cannot be teaching that it makes other liquid impure.

steps.title: רבינא: the wording of the verse itself rules it out
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a second reason. If both 'יִטְמָא's meant 'makes liquids impure,' the תורה could have combined them into one sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: From the פסוק itself you also cannot say that 'יִטְמָא' means making liquids impure. If the 'יִטְמָא' at the end meant making liquids impure, then the 'יִטְמָא' at the beginning also means making liquids impure. If so, the תורה should have combined them and written: 'From all food that may be eaten, on which water came, and every drink that may be drunk in any vessel, shall be impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different proof, taken from the wording of the פסוק itself. He shows that if both halves taught the same thing, the תורה should have joined them into one sentence with one 'יִטְמָא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'יִטְמָא' twice, once about food and once about drink. If both meant 'makes liquids impure,' the two cases could have shared one word. The extra word tells us that each 'יִטְמָא' teaches something different.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it combine them and write them together

steps.confusionAlert: 'רֵישָׁא' and 'סֵיפָא' here mean the first and second halves of the פסוק, not of a משנה. The first half is about food and the second half is about drink.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
From the verse itself, too,
you cannot say that 'shall be impure' means
making liquids impure.
For if it enters your mind
that 'shall be impure' of the end of the verse means
making liquids impure,
then 'shall be impure' of the beginning also means
making liquids impure.
So let the verse combine them and write them together:
'From all food that may be eaten,
on which water has come,
and every drink that may be drunk
in any vessel, shall be impure.'
phrases.notes: If the two verses were joined into one, it would say 'יִטְמָא' only once.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: מִגּוּפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to Step 14. רב פפא used general logic, while רבינא uses the wording of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled 'יִטְמָא' would be unnecessary if both halves meant the same thing.

steps.title: Two words, two lessons: liquids and foods
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה wrote 'יִטְמָא' twice, the first teaches making liquids impure and the second teaches making foods impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'shall be impure' twice? Rather, the 'shall be impure' at the beginning teaches making liquids impure. The 'shall be impure' at the end teaches making foods impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finishes his proof. Each 'יִטְמָא' teaches its own lesson, and the second one teaches that liquids make foods impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'יִטְמָא', in the food half, teaches that impure food makes liquids impure. The second 'יִטְמָא', in the drink half, teaches that impure liquid makes food impure. This confirms the reading from Step 11.
steps.whatToRemember: The two 'יִטְמָא's in the פסוק teach two different lessons. Food makes liquids impure, and liquids make food impure.

phrases.english: Why do I need 'shall be impure' twice?
Rather, 'shall be impure' of the beginning means
making liquids impure,
and 'shall be impure' of the end means
making foods impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that רבינא began in Step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second 'יִטְמָא' teaches that impure liquids make foods impure.

steps.title: Maybe the word teaches that liquids make vessels impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another option. Perhaps the second 'יִטְמָא' teaches that liquids make vessels impure, not foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it teaches making vessels impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Perhaps the extra 'יִטְמָא' teaches that liquids make vessels impure, rather than foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא proved that the second 'יִטְמָא' must teach something new. But he did not prove that the new thing is food. Vessels are another possible target, and that would weaken the proof for foods.

phrases.english: But say it teaches making vessels impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 17 by offering a different thing for the second 'יִטְמָא' to teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the second 'יִטְמָא' teaches making foods impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word could teach that liquids make vessels impure instead of foods.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: liquids cannot make vessels impure
steps.stepSummary: A vessel makes liquid impure but cannot make another vessel impure. Liquids that only became impure from a vessel surely cannot make vessels impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it a קל וחומר? An impure vessel makes liquid impure, yet it does not make another vessel impure. Liquids that became impure only because of a vessel are weaker, so surely they should not make vessels impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the vessel option using a קל וחומר. It shows that liquids are too weak to make vessels impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessel is the stronger item, since it is the source of the liquid's impurity. Even the vessel cannot make another vessel impure. So the weaker liquid surely cannot make a vessel impure, and the 'יִטְמָא' must teach foods.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one (a fortiori)

steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms the final reading. Impure liquids make foods impure, but they do not make vessels impure on a Torah level.

phrases.english: But isn't it a קל וחומר?
Just as a vessel, which makes liquid impure,
does not make another vessel impure,
then liquids that became impure because of a vessel,
is it not logical
that they should not make vessels impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר logic that rules out the alternative reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second 'יִטְמָא' might teach that liquids make vessels impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liquids are weaker than vessels, so they cannot make vessels impure. The 'יִטְמָא' teaches that liquids make foods impure.

steps.title: Maybe liquids made impure by a creeping creature can make vessels impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 19. Perhaps only liquids made impure by a כלי cannot make vessels impure, while liquids made impure by a שרץ can.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: liquids cannot make a vessel impure only when they became impure from a vessel. Liquids that became impure from a שרץ really should make vessels impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It tries again to read the second יִטְמָא as 'liquids make vessels impure,' this time for liquids that touched a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 argued that a vessel cannot make another vessel impure, so liquids that got their impurity from a vessel cannot either. That logic only works when the liquid's impurity came from a vessel. A שרץ is a much stronger source of impurity (an אב הטומאה), so liquids it touched might be strong enough to make vessels impure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...': introduces another possible reading that challenges the last answer
Liquids that became impure because they touched an impure vessel
Liquids that became impure because they touched a שרץ directly
A dead creeping creature, a strong source of impurity (אַב הַטֻּמְאָה)
'So too' / 'indeed': here, 'they really should' make vessels impure

phrases.english: But say: when do they not make impure?
phrases.notes: 'They' means impure liquids, which cannot make vessels impure.

phrases.english: Only liquids that come to impurity because of a vessel.
phrases.notes: This is the case covered by the logic of step 19.

phrases.english: But liquids that come to impurity because of a creeping creature,
indeed they should make vessels impure!
phrases.notes: So perhaps the second יִטְמָא teaches this, and not foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It narrows the answer of step 19 to liquids impure from a vessel, then revives the challenge of step 18 for liquids impure from a שרץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 19 that impure liquids can never make vessels impure, which supports reading the second יִטְמָא as foods.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 19's reasoning applies only to liquids impure from a vessel. Liquids impure from a stronger source, a שרץ, could still make vessels impure, so the second יִטְמָא could teach that instead of foods.

steps.title: The verse never speaks of liquids made impure by a creeping creature
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not talking about liquids impure from a שרץ. Its liquids became impure through a vessel, so the challenge fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are liquids that became impure from a שרץ written in the פסוק at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a short rhetorical question. The פסוק never mentions liquids that touched a שרץ directly, so it cannot be teaching a law about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the שרץ falls into a clay vessel, and the liquid becomes impure because it is inside that vessel. So the liquid in the פסוק is always 'liquid impure from a vessel.' Step 19 already showed that such liquid cannot make vessels impure. That leaves only one reading: the second יִטְמָא teaches that liquids make foods impure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Are they written?': a rhetorical question meaning the פסוק does not mention this case
A clay vessel: in the פסוק, the שרץ falls into one and makes its contents impure

steps.whatToRemember: The liquids in the פסוק became impure through a vessel, and such liquids cannot make vessels impure. So the second יִטְמָא must teach that liquids make foods impure.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say that liquids touched by a שרץ can make vessels impure. It only says the פסוק is not discussing that case, so the extra יִטְמָא cannot be read as teaching it.

phrases.english: Liquids that come to impurity because of a creeping creature,
phrases.notes: Quoting the case raised in the challenge.

phrases.english: are they written in the verse?
phrases.notes: No. The verse's liquids became impure through the clay vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁקִין הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרֶץ מִי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge of step 20 by showing that its case is not in the פסוק at all.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: the case raised by the challenge is not what the פסוק describes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second יִטְמָא might teach that liquids impure from a שרץ make vessels impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only discusses liquids impure from a vessel, which cannot make vessels impure. So the second יִטְמָא teaches that liquids make foods impure, as concluded in step 17.
